title: Outcomes, Not Outputs
intro: Outputs are what you ship. Outcomes are what changes because of it.

learn.title: The build trap
learn.text:
Teams measured on **features shipped** keep shipping and stop checking whether anything changed.

A product has no value on its own. Value is what it does for customers; the business gains only when that happens.

try.q: Which of these is an outcome?
options: More teams finish setup in week one
Every single roadmap date met on time this year
try.explain: It describes a change in customer behaviour.

learn.title: Three kinds of metric
learn.text:
**Business outcome:** revenue, retention. Too far away for one team.
**Product outcome:** customer behaviour in the product. **The best fit for discovery.**
**Traction metric:** use of one feature. Narrows the solutions to one.

try.q: Which metric suits a discovery team best?
try.explain: The team can move it, and many solutions could.

learn.title: From strategy to the team
learn.text:
**Strategic intent:** a few goals for one to two years.
**Product initiatives:** customer problems to solve.
**Options:** solutions, treated as bets.

Leaders set the why. Teams own the how.

try.q: In this cascade, what are solutions treated as?
try.explain: A solution is a bet that it will move the outcome.

learn.title: Four risks
learn.text:
**Value:** will they choose it?
**Usability:** can they use it?
**Feasibility:** can we build it?
**Viability:** does it work for the business, including legal and ethics?

Check them before building.

try.q: “Does it break our pricing or compliance rules?” Which risk is that?
try.explain: Viability covers whether the business can support it.

options: Building before the design is final
test.explain: Outputs become the goal instead of the change they should cause.

options: Weekly uses of the export button
Share of teams still active 30 days after signing up
test.explain: It tracks one feature, which suits optimising that feature.

test.q: Why is a business outcome a poor discovery goal?
options: Too many teams and forces move it
It cannot be measured precisely enough to be useful
test.explain: A team can’t see its own effect on it.

test.q: Someone asks for a feature. What should you ask first?
options: How many engineers it will need to build it
test.explain: If nobody can say, it is an output looking for a reason.

test.q: Who is usually best placed to judge feasibility?
test.explain: They know the time, skills and technology available.

test.q: What should leaders set in outcome-led work?
test.explain: Teams own how to reach it.
